To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction sensitivity is affected by the converter’s input and output impedances, and the converter’s control method affects the impedance characteristics of the converter.
the impedance-based interactions are affected by the converter control method and the interaction sensitivity can therefore be predicted based on the control method and the converter topology.
the interaction sensitivity is a function of the converter’s impedance-type internal parameters, which are determined by the control method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the analysis of impedance-based interactions in distributed dc–dc converters, where the interaction sensitivity is analyzed in terms of the converter internal parameters.
the impedance-based interactions and their effect on the transient behavior of the distributed dc– dc systems

the following aspects: • The effect of different control methods on impedance-based interactions in a distributed dc–dc system • A new set of impedance parameters to characterize impedance-based interactions
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction sensitivity can significantly be influenced by choosing a proper control method.

a control method that has a low impedance at the input and output of the converter, i.e., a control method that provides a low input impedance and a high output impedance, would be the best choice for the design of a distributed dc–dc system.
the control method affects significantly on the interaction sensitivity of a buck converter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction sensitivity can always be characterized by the same set of impedance parameters and formulas regardless the control method.
the control method is the most important design parameter for the converter stability and performance.
the interaction sensitivity can only be decreased by reducing the converter’s impedance-type internal parameters, which is a very challenging task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction sensitivity is not a constant property of the converter, but depends significantly on the applied control method and the operating conditions.
the control method affects the impedance-type internal parameters of the converter and, therefore, the sensitivity to different interaction types.
the sensitivity to different impedance-type interactions can be significantly reduced by using a proper control method, even though the converter itself is not changed.
